summary: The RTP/AVP profile underlies many other profiles. This document updates RFC 3551 to reflect changes in audio codec usage by removing DVI4 from the recommended codecs. The change carries through to the profiles built on RTP/AVP.

eli5.summary: An old audio format is no longer a good pick, so it is taken off the recommended list.

questions: dvi4 removed from recommended rtp codecs
why was dvi4 removed from rtp avp
what audio codec must rtp avp support
subtitle: The RTP audio profile stops recommending DVI4 and keeps only PCMU as the baseline codec.

tldr.problem: RFC 3551 said audio applications SHOULD be able to send and receive PCMU and DVI4, but many RTP deployments do not support DVI4 and much more modern codecs are available.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC rewrites one paragraph of RFC 3551 so that only payload type 0 (PCMU) remains in the minimum recommendation, and adds a sentence saying some environments necessitate PCMU.
tldr.outcome: The change carries through to the profiles built on RTP/AVP. It updates RFC 3551.

today: RFC 7007 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3551. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why DVI4 Is Dropped
sections.content:
RFC 3551 says audio applications under the RTP/AVP profile SHOULD be able to send and receive PCMU and DVI4. In practice, many RTP deployments do not support DVI4, and there is little reason to use it when much more modern codecs are available.

This document removes the SHOULD for DVI4. By extension it also updates the profiles that build on RTP/AVP: RTP/SAVP (RFC 3711), RTP/AVPF (RFC 4585) and RTP/SAVPF (RFC 5124).
sections.eli5: Almost nobody uses the old audio format any more, so it is taken off the list of things every program should know.

sections.title: The Replacement Text
sections.content:
The update changes the final paragraph of Section 6 of RFC 3551. It replaces "payload types 0 (PCMU) and 5 (DVI4)" with "payload type 0 (PCMU)" and adds a final sentence: "Some environments necessitate support for PCMU".

The resulting rule is that audio applications SHOULD, at a minimum, be able to send and/or receive payload type 0 (PCMU). This allows interoperability without format negotiation and ensures successful negotiation with a conference control protocol.
sections.eli5: The rule now names just one audio format that every program should be ready to use, so two programs can always talk to each other.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document does not introduce any new security considerations for RFC 3551.
sections.eli5: Crossing a format off the list does not make anything less safe.
